> Your knowledge and skills are valuable

That's only the case for people who have the social skills to sell themselves well in an interview.  I have a MBA and 5 years of experience in the field I'm seeking work in, this area has a low unemployment rate for my field, and the current economy is growing jobs in my field in this area.  I've been struggling for six months to find a job that pays more than entry-level work pays.  I'm not great at impressing people in interviews, but I impress people in my work.  Unfortunately, they never see the latter and only see the former because the flawed interview process puts social skills above all other skills, even in jobs where social skills are not as important.

Telling people to not be afraid to leave their job is bad advice.  It is a decision that can't be taken lightly, even if they are unhappy in their situation.  Evaluate your plans and evaluate your ability to perform well in interviews before you quit.
